model_tenancy_act.notified_by: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, Government of India
model_tenancy_act.summary: The Model Tenancy Act, 2021 aims to balance the interests of landlords and tenants by establishing a fast-track dispute resolution mechanism, creating Rent Authority, Rent Court and Rent Tribunal. It seeks to unlock vacant properties by instilling confidence in property owners and to create adequate rental housing stock for all income segments.

sections.title: Definitions
sections.description: In this Act: 'landlord' means a person who for the time being is receiving or is entitled to receive rent in respect of any premises; 'tenant' means a person who is paying or is liable to pay rent for any premises under a tenancy agreement; 'Rent Authority' means the authority appointed under Section 4; 'premises' means any building or part of building let or to be let on rent.

sections.title: Rent Authority
sections.description: The appropriate Government shall, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint an officer, not below the rank of Deputy Collector, to be the Rent Authority for the purpose of this Act within the local area specified in such notification. The Rent Authority shall be responsible for registration of tenancy agreements and adjudication of disputes between landlord and tenant.

sections.title: Submission of tenancy agreement to Rent Authority
sections.description: The landlord and tenant shall, within two months of executing a tenancy agreement, inform the Rent Authority by submitting a copy of the tenancy agreement in such form and manner as may be prescribed. The Rent Authority shall, on receipt of the tenancy agreement, issue a unique identification number to the landlord and tenant within seven working days.

sections.title: Conditions of tenancy
sections.description: The landlord and tenant may agree to vary the conditions of tenancy by executing a new or revised tenancy agreement and submit a copy thereof to the Rent Authority within two months of execution.

sections.title: Security deposit
sections.description: The landlord may collect a security deposit from the tenant at the time of entering into a tenancy agreement. The security deposit shall not exceed two months rent in case of residential premises and six months rent in case of non-residential premises. The security deposit shall be refunded by the landlord to the tenant within one month of vacation of premises after making any lawful deductions.

sections.title: Revision of rent
sections.description: The rent shall be revised as per the tenancy agreement. In the absence of any provision in the tenancy agreement, the landlord shall give at least three months advance notice in writing to the tenant before revising the rent.

sections.title: Landlord not to interfere with amenities
sections.description: No landlord shall, without just or sufficient cause, cut off or withhold any essential supply or service in respect of the premises held by the tenant. Essential supply means supply of water, electricity, sanitation facilities including toilets, parking space, communication infrastructure such as cable television, broadband or any other service as agreed in the tenancy agreement. Any landlord who contravenes the provisions of this section shall be liable to pay the tenant a sum equivalent to the amount of rent for each day during which the essential supplies are withheld.

sections.title: Vacation of premises on expiry of tenancy
sections.description: On the expiry of the period of tenancy, the tenant shall vacate the premises. In case of failure to vacate, the landlord may approach the Rent Court for eviction. During the period the tenant continues to occupy premises after expiry, he shall be liable to pay enhanced rent - double the monthly rent for first two months and four times the monthly rent thereafter.

sections.title: Rent Court
sections.description: The State Government shall, by notification in the Official Gazette, establish one or more Rent Courts for the purpose of this Act. The Rent Court shall be presided over by an officer not below the rank of Additional District Magistrate or equivalent. The Rent Court shall decide applications within sixty days of filing.

sections.title: Rent Tribunal
sections.description: The State Government shall, by notification in the Official Gazette, establish one or more Rent Tribunals. The Rent Tribunal shall be presided over by a person who is or has been a District Judge. Appeals from the Rent Court shall lie to the Rent Tribunal. The Rent Tribunal shall decide appeals within ninety days.

key_provisions: Written rental agreement mandatory for all tenancies
Security deposit capped at 2 months rent for residential premises
Security deposit capped at 6 months rent for non-residential/commercial premises
Landlord cannot cut electricity, water or other essential supplies
Three months advance notice required for rent revision (if not in agreement)
Unique identification number issued by Rent Authority for each tenancy
Eviction possible through Rent Court on expiry of tenancy
Double rent payable for first 2 months of overstay; 4x rent thereafter
Rent Court to decide disputes within 60 days
Rent Tribunal as appellate body; appeals decided within 90 days
Landlord must refund security deposit within 1 month of vacation
Tenant cannot sub-let without written consent of landlord
model_tenancy_act.disputes_process: Rent Authority → Rent Court → Rent Tribunal → High Court

Maharashtra.applicable_areas: Entire State of Maharashtra including Mumbai Metropolitan Region, Pune, Nagpur, and other municipal areas
key_provisions: Standard rent concept: landlord cannot charge more than standard rent
Tenant cannot be evicted except on specific grounds (non-payment of rent, subletting without permission, nuisance, etc.)
Landlord must give proper notice before filing eviction proceedings
Permitted increases in rent linked to property tax and cost of living index
Premises Act 1947 applies to certain categories of tenancy in Mumbai
Protection to tenants who have been in occupation for long periods
Maharashtra.court: Small Causes Court, Mumbai (for Mumbai); Civil Court for rest of Maharashtra
Maharashtra.standard_rent: Determined by Rent Controller based on type and location of property
Maharashtra.notes: Maharashtra has one of the oldest rent control regimes in India. The 1999 Act replaced the earlier Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act 1947. Pagdi (premium) system prevalent in older Mumbai tenancies where tenant pays lump sum and low monthly rent. The Act does not apply to new constructions (post-1999 in most areas under the amended provisions).

Karnataka.applicable_areas: All urban areas in Karnataka; the Act applies to premises in municipal limits
key_provisions: Landlord must register the tenancy agreement
Standard rent fixation by Rent Controller
Grounds for eviction include non-payment of rent, subletting, required for own use, demolition, etc.
Landlord cannot enhance rent by more than 10% per annum
Advance rent (deposit) regulated - maximum up to 10 months rent in some areas
Sitting tenants protected from arbitrary eviction
Karnataka.court: Court of Rent Controller (Special Courts under the Act)
Karnataka.standard_rent: Rent Controller fixes standard rent; annual increase capped at 10%
Karnataka.notes: Karnataka has adopted Model Tenancy Act framework partially. For new residential leases in IT corridor areas like Whitefield, Sarjapur, HSR Layout, market rents prevail. The 1999 Act primarily applies to old rent-controlled premises in Bengaluru.

Delhi.applicable_areas: National Capital Territory of Delhi; applies only to properties with monthly rent up to Rs 3,500 - other properties governed by Transfer of Property Act
key_provisions: Only applies to properties with contractual rent up to Rs 3,500 per month
Properties above Rs 3,500 monthly rent governed by Transfer of Property Act 1882 and general contract law
Landlord can increase standard rent by 10% every 3 years
Eviction grounds: non-payment, subletting, nuisance, bona fide personal need, reconstruction
Tenant must deposit rent in court if landlord refuses to accept
Disputes heard by Rent Controller (Additional Rent Controller, District)
Delhi.standard_rent: Rent Act only for properties under Rs 3,500/month; others by market rate
Delhi.notes: The Delhi Rent Act 1995 has a very narrow application due to the Rs 3,500 rent ceiling, making most modern properties fall outside its purview and governed by general property law. Delhi adopted the Model Tenancy Act in 2021 and is in process of implementing it.

Tamil Nadu.act_name: Tamil Nadu Regulation of Rights and Responsibilities of Landlords and Tenants Act, 2017
key_provisions: Mandatory written and registered tenancy agreement
Security deposit maximum 5 months rent for residential; for commercial - as agreed
Landlord must issue receipt for rent paid
90 days notice required by landlord for eviction
Tenant shall pay rent within 15 days of due date
Rent Tribunal for appeals within 30 days of Rent Court order
Tamil Nadu was first state to enact a comprehensive modern tenancy act
Tamil Nadu.court: Rent Authority (District Collector or designate); Rent Tribunal for appeals
Tamil Nadu.standard_rent: Market rent; no rent control under the 2017 Act
Tamil Nadu.notes: Tamil Nadu was the first state to enact a comprehensive tenancy regulation act after the central government proposed reforms. It aligns largely with the Model Tenancy Act approach but predates it. Advance (deposit) culture is strong in Tamil Nadu especially in Chennai - advance up to 10-12 months was common but the 2017 Act caps it at 5 months.

Gujarat.act_name: Gujarat Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948 (for agricultural); Gujarat Rent Control Act, 1947 (for urban)
Gujarat.applicable_areas: Urban areas of Gujarat for rent control; the State is also implementing Model Tenancy Act
key_provisions: Standard rent concept for old tenancies under 1947 Act
New tenancies post-liberalisation governed more by market forces and Transfer of Property Act
Eviction proceedings before Mamlatdar court for some tenancy categories
Tenant protected if paying rent regularly and not subletting without permission
Gujarat adopted Model Tenancy Act with minor modifications in 2022
Security deposit typically 2-3 months for residential under Model Tenancy Act norms
Gujarat.court: Small Causes Court (Ahmedabad, Surat); Civil Court in other districts
Gujarat.standard_rent: Varies; old properties under rent control, new properties at market rate
Gujarat.notes: Gujarat has a bifurcated system - old properties under stringent rent control, new constructions governed by market forces and the recently adopted Model Tenancy Act framework. Ahmedabad and Surat have significant old rent-controlled tenancies.

Rajasthan.applicable_areas: Entire State of Rajasthan including Jaipur, Jodhpur, Udaipur, Kota and other urban areas
key_provisions: Tenancy agreement to be in writing
Standard rent to be fixed by Rent Tribunal
Eviction only on grounds specified in Act: non-payment, subletting, nuisance, personal need
Landlord can seek possession for bona fide personal or family use
Appeal from Rent Tribunal to High Court
Rajasthan adopted provisions broadly aligned with Model Tenancy Act
Security deposit regulated; market-based in practice
Rajasthan.court: Rent Tribunal (Presided by District Judge); appeal to High Court
Rajasthan.standard_rent: Market-based with standard rent fixation available before Rent Tribunal
Rajasthan.notes: Rajasthan's 2001 Act is relatively modernised compared to older state rent control laws. Jaipur has seen significant real estate growth with private residential leases largely governed by market dynamics.

Andhra Pradesh.act_name: Andhra Pradesh Buildings (Lease, Rent and Eviction) Control Act, 1960
Andhra Pradesh.applicable_areas: Urban areas of Andhra Pradesh including Vijayawada, Visakhapatnam, Tirupati and other municipalities
key_provisions: Standard rent and permitted increases regulated by the Rent Controller
Fair rent fixation on application by either landlord or tenant
Eviction grounds: default in rent payment (2+ months), subletting, causing nuisance, landlord personal use, demolition
Compensation payable to tenant on eviction for personal use
Advance (deposit) regulated under the Act
Small Cause Courts and subordinate civil courts exercise jurisdiction
Andhra Pradesh.court: Rent Controller (Special Rent Court); appeal to District Court
Andhra Pradesh.standard_rent: Fair rent fixed by Rent Controller based on building value and amenities
Andhra Pradesh.notes: Andhra Pradesh retained the 1960 Act post-bifurcation from Telangana. The Act applies to buildings in urban areas. Visakhapatnam being a growing IT and port city has seen increased demand for residential and commercial leases beyond the rent-controlled framework.

Telangana.act_name: Telangana Regulation of Residential Buildings and Tenancies Act, 2021 (and legacy Andhra Pradesh Buildings Act 1960)
Telangana.applicable_areas: State of Telangana including Hyderabad, Secunderabad, Cyberabad and other urban areas
key_provisions: New Act of 2021 introduced for residential buildings aligning with Model Tenancy Act
Mandatory online registration of tenancy agreements through TRNC (Telangana Real Estate Regulatory Commission)
Security deposit regulated: maximum 2 months for residential
Three months notice required for eviction
Landlord prohibited from disconnecting utilities to coerce eviction
Legacy Andhra Pradesh Buildings Act 1960 continues for pre-existing commercial tenancies
Rent Court and Rent Authority established under the 2021 Act
Telangana.court: Rent Court; appeal to Rent Tribunal under the 2021 Act
Telangana.standard_rent: Market-based; no rent control under 2021 Act
Telangana.notes: Telangana adopted the Model Tenancy Act framework early with the 2021 Act. Hyderabad is India's major IT hub, and rentals in Madhapur, Gachibowli, Kondapur follow market rates entirely under the new framework. Advance payment culture is transitioning from high deposits (5-10 months) to the regulated 2-month norm.

West Bengal.applicable_areas: Entire State of West Bengal including Kolkata, Howrah and other urban areas
key_provisions: Tenancy agreements governed by 1997 Act
Standard rent concept: landlord entitled to reasonable return on property
Permitted increases in rent at prescribed intervals
Eviction on grounds: non-payment of rent, subletting without permission, nuisance, bona fide need of landlord
Twelve months notice required for eviction for personal use
Controller of Rents or designated court for disputes
Kolkata has significant stock of old rent-controlled premises from Calcutta Rent Control Act 1950 (now superseded)
West Bengal.court: Special Rent Controller; Civil Court for some matters; High Court for appeals
West Bengal.standard_rent: Standard rent determined by Controller on application; includes legitimate land and construction costs
West Bengal.notes: West Bengal has one of the more tenant-friendly rent control regimes. The long notice period for eviction for personal use (12 months) gives tenants significant protection. Kolkata's old buildings have many legacy rent-controlled tenancies where tenants pay very low rents. New constructions and high-end localities follow market rates.

Uttar Pradesh.act_name: Uttar Pradesh Urban Buildings (Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Act, 1972
Uttar Pradesh.applicable_areas: Urban areas of Uttar Pradesh including Lucknow, Agra, Kanpur, Varanasi, Allahabad (Prayagraj) and other cities
key_provisions: Allotment system: Prescribed Authority (usually District Magistrate) allocates vacant premises
Rent Controller approves rent and tenancy terms
Standard rent cannot exceed amount sanctioned under the Act
Eviction grounds specified: non-payment, subletting, nuisance, personal use, material alteration
Tenant entitled to make repairs and deduct from rent if landlord fails to maintain
Strict restriction on release of premises from rent control
Act does not apply to premises built after a cut-off date (1985 in most areas)
Uttar Pradesh.court: Prescribed Authority (Tehsildar/SDM level); appeal to Rent Control Tribunal; further appeal to High Court
Uttar Pradesh.standard_rent: Standard rent fixed by Rent Controller; no enhancement except in prescribed circumstances
Uttar Pradesh.notes: The UP Act has a unique allotment system making it one of the most regulated tenancy regimes. The Act does not apply to buildings constructed after 1985 (as per the exemption provision), meaning modern properties in Lucknow, NOIDA, Ghaziabad are governed by Transfer of Property Act and market rents. The old Act remains relevant for pre-1985 constructions in city centres.
